newsitem.title: USA: Pacific says to exit Solium, take charge.
newsitem.headline: Pacific says to exit Solium, take charge.

text.p: Pacific Scientific Co said Wednesday it will seek a strategic buyer for its Solium technology and equipment and will phase out its Solium subsidiary, resulting in a one-time charge of about $12 million net of taxes in the first quarter.
Solium will be reclassified as a discontinued operation on financial statements, it said.
Pacific Scientific said that over the past two years, Solium operations have resulted in a $0.94 per share charge against the company's reported earnings.

After exiting Solium, the company's earnings from continuing operations will be restated higher to $1.15 in 1995 and $0.81 in 1996, compared with the previously reported $1.01 for 1995 and $0.01 for 1996, the company said.
At year-end 1996, Pacific Scientific had working capital of $83 million and a debt-to-capital ratio of 42 percent.
Pacific Scientific said the Solium discontinuance is not expected to adversely affect the company's ability to finance operations and fund planned capital expenditures.
Pacific Scientific manufactures, designs and markets electrical safety equipment. The Solium division primarily makes electronic ballasts.
